tools.name: calc_rent_schedule
tools.description: Build a base-rent schedule from commencement date, term, area, starting $/SF/yr, escalations (percent or fixed $/SF), and abated months. Lease months run from the commencement day-of-month with no calendar proration (warns when commencement is mid-month). Returns rent steps, totals, expiration date, and a calculation trace. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.rent_schedule@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 120 for ten years.

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5.

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

rate.description: Bump as a decimal, e.g. 0.03 for 3%. Bumps compound.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

include_monthly.description: Include a month-by-month table (can be long).

tools.name: calc_net_effective_rent
tools.description: Compute effective rent, straight-line net effective rent, and discounted net effective rent ($/SF/yr) after free rent, TI allowance, leasing commissions, and other landlord concessions. Rent is monthly in advance from the commencement day (no calendar proration), discounted at annual rate ÷ 12. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.net_effective_rent@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 120 for ten years.

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5.

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

include_monthly.description: Include a month-by-month table (can be long).

schedule.description: The lease's base-rent terms (same input as calc_rent_schedule).

ti_allowance_psf.description: Landlord-funded tenant improvement allowance, USD per SF, paid once at commencement (not per year).

leasing_commissions.description: Total leasing commissions paid by landlord, USD.

other_concessions.description: Any other landlord concessions paid at commencement (moving allowance, buyout), USD.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08 (monthly rate = annual ÷ 12); 0 gives the undiscounted (straight-line) NER.

tools.name: calc_compare_proposals
tools.description: Rank 2–20 lease proposals with different terms, sizes, free rent, TI, concessions, and operating-expense structures (gross, NNN, base year, expense stop, with opex growth) on one discounted $/SF/yr basis, per rentable or usable SF (load factor): effective occupancy cost (tenant perspective) or discounted net effective rent after landlord-borne opex and optional pre-commencement downtime (landlord perspective). Cash flows monthly in advance at annual rate ÷ 12; warns when the usable-SF ranking differs and when terms differ. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.compare_proposals@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

perspective.description: Whose economics to rank on: tenant (effective occupancy cost, lower is better) or landlord (discounted net effective rent, higher is better).

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08, applied to every proposal (monthly rate = annual ÷ 12, cash flows at the start of each month).

area_basis.description: Area the $/SF/yr metric is divided by: rentable (schedule.area_sf, the default) or usable (each proposal's usable_sf, or area_sf ÷ load_factor). Rents and expenses stay quoted per rentable SF; use usable when proposals have different load factors and the tenant needs a fixed usable area.

name.description: Unique label for the proposal, e.g. building name.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

term_months.description: Lease term in months, e.g. 120 for ten years.

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5.

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

rate.description: Bump as a decimal, e.g. 0.03 for 3%. Bumps compound.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

include_monthly.description: Include a month-by-month table (can be long).

schedule.description: Base-rent terms of this proposal (same input as calc_rent_schedule); schedule.area_sf is the rentable area.

usable_sf.description: Usable square feet of this proposal (at most schedule.area_sf). Give this or load_factor, not both; required for area_basis usable.

load_factor.description: Rentable ÷ usable area, e.g. 1.15 (usable_sf = area_sf ÷ load_factor). Give this or usable_sf, not both.

ti_allowance_psf.description: TI allowance paid by the landlord, USD per rentable SF, once at commencement (not per year).

other_concessions.description: Other cash concessions to the tenant at commencement (moving allowance, buyout), USD.

leasing_commissions.description: Leasing commissions paid by landlord at commencement, USD (landlord perspective only).

operating_expenses.description: Operating-expense structure of this proposal: gross, nnn, base_year, or expense_stop, with a lease-year-1 estimate and growth. Tenant perspective adds what the tenant pays; landlord perspective deducts what the landlord bears. Omit to price no operating expenses (as before).

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses the landlord pays, $/SF/yr in lease year 1 (used in the landlord perspective; the tenant pays none).

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual).

oneOf.description: Full-service gross: the landlord pays all operating expenses; the tenant pays none beyond base rent.

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses (CAM, taxes, insurance) for lease year 1, $/SF/yr on rentable area.

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual).

oneOf.description: Net (NNN): the tenant pays all operating expenses, estimated at expense_psf_annual in lease year 1.

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses (CAM, taxes, insurance) for lease year 1, $/SF/yr on rentable area.

base_year_psf_annual.description: Base-year operating expenses, $/SF/yr. Defaults to expense_psf_annual (the base year is lease year 1).

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual).

oneOf.description: Gross with a base year: the tenant pays operating expenses above the base-year amount.

expense_psf_annual.description: Estimated operating expenses (CAM, taxes, insurance) for lease year 1, $/SF/yr on rentable area.

stop_psf_annual.description: Expense stop, $/SF/yr: the tenant pays operating expenses above this fixed amount.

growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth of operating expenses as a decimal, e.g. 0.03, compounding each lease year from commencement (lease year 1 is expense_psf_annual).

oneOf.description: Gross with an expense stop: the tenant pays operating expenses above a fixed $/SF/yr stop.

additional_costs_psf_annual.description: Other costs the tenant pays on top of base rent, flat $/SF/yr on rentable area (tenant perspective only), e.g. parking. Prefer operating_expenses for opex pass-throughs, which can grow and follow a base year or stop.

tenant_upfront_costs.description: Tenant's own costs at commencement not covered by allowances (TI overage, moving), USD.

downtime_months.description: Landlord perspective: vacant months before this proposal commences (no rent; the landlord carries lease-year-1 operating expenses if operating_expenses is given). The metric is then the level monthly amount over downtime plus term. Ignored for the tenant.

tools.name: calc_percentage_rent
tools.description: Percentage (overage) rent for a lease year: net sales after exclusions over a natural or fixed breakpoint, prorated for partial years, less amounts already paid. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.percentage_rent@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

gross_sales.description: Gross sales reported for the lease year (or partial year), USD.

sales_exclusions.description: Sales excluded by the lease (returns, sales tax, gift cards, employee sales, …), USD.

base_rent_annual.description: Annual base rent, USD per year (a full lease year, even for a partial period); used for the natural breakpoint.

breakpoint.description: Breakpoint above which percentage rent applies. Default: natural.

oneOf.description: Natural breakpoint = annual base rent ÷ rate.

amount.description: Annual sales breakpoint stated in the lease, USD.

oneOf.description: Artificial (fixed) breakpoint stated in the lease.

period_fraction.description: Fraction of a full lease year covered (e.g. 0.5 for a six-month partial year). Prorates the breakpoint.

percentage_rent_paid.description: Percentage rent already paid during the period, USD.

tools.name: calc_cam_reconciliation
tools.description: Reconcile a tenant's annual CAM charge: exclusions, occupancy gross-up of variable expenses, pro rata share, controllable-expense caps (compounding_from_base, simple_from_base, year_over_year), an admin fee (before or after the cap, inside or outside it, with per-line exclusions), base year or expense stop, partial-year occupancy (move-in/move-out prorates share, cap, and base by days), and estimates paid. Returns balance due and a full trace with order-of-operations warnings. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.cam_reconciliation@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

year.description: Calendar or lease year being reconciled.

category.description: Expense line as named in the operating statement, e.g. "janitorial".

amount.description: Building-level actual expense for the year, USD.

controllable.description: Subject to the cap. Taxes, insurance, and utilities are typically uncontrollable.

recoverable.description: Excluded expenses (capital items, landlord-only costs) are dropped entirely.

variable.description: Varies with occupancy, so eligible for gross-up (janitorial, utilities, management fee).

admin_fee_applies.description: Included in the admin_fee base. Set false for lines the lease excludes from the fee (often taxes, insurance, utilities, or a management fee already charged).

expenses.description: Building operating expense lines for the year.

gross_up.description: Gross up variable expenses to the target occupancy when actual occupancy is lower. Omit if the lease has no gross-up.

actual_occupancy.description: Average occupancy for the year, e.g. 0.82.

target_occupancy.description: Gross-up occupancy stated in the lease (commonly 0.95 or 1.0).

structure.description: Expense structure from the lease. Default: net.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its full share of recoverable expenses (NNN / net).

base_year_expenses.description: Total building recoverable expenses in the base year, already grossed up, USD.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over base-year expenses.

stop_amount.description: Building-level expense stop, USD per year.

oneOf.description: Tenant pays its share of the excess over a fixed expense stop.

cap.description: Cap on the tenant's share of controllable expenses. Omit if the lease has no cap.

method.description: compounding_from_base: reference × (1+rate)^years (often called cumulative, compounding). simple_from_base: reference × (1 + rate × years) (cumulative, non-compounding). year_over_year: prior year's capped amount × (1+rate) (non-cumulative). Map the lease language to one of these explicitly.

rate.description: Annual cap as a decimal, e.g. 0.05.

reference_amount.description: Tenant's share of controllable expenses in the reference year: the base year for *_from_base, or the prior year's capped amount for year_over_year, USD.

years_elapsed.description: Years since the base year (required for `*_from_base`).

admin_fee.description: Administrative fee the lease adds to the tenant's share. Omit if the lease has none.

rate.description: Administrative or management fee as a decimal of the fee base, e.g. 0.15 for 15%. The base is the tenant's share of recoverable lines with admin_fee_applies (after gross-up).

applied.description: Fee on controllable lines computed on the tenant's share before the cap (before_cap) or on the capped amount (after_cap). Fees on uncontrollable lines are never capped. Irrelevant without a cap.

capped.description: True when the fee on controllable lines counts toward the controllable cap (controllable share plus fee may not exceed the cap limit); false adds it outside the cap.

occupancy.description: Partial-year occupancy: the tenant's share, cap limit, and base-year or stop deduction are prorated by occupied days ÷ period days (both inclusive), so a full-year cap and base are not applied to a part year. Omit for a full year.

move_in_date.description: Date the tenant's share starts within the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_start_date.

move_out_date.description: Last day of the tenant's share within the period, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to period_end_date.

period_start_date.description: First day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to January 1 of year; set it for a lease year.

period_end_date.description: Last day of the reconciliation period, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 366 days after the start). Defaults to December 31 of year.

estimates_paid.description: Estimated CAM payments the tenant made during the year, USD (total for the year, not monthly).

tools.name: calc_debt_sizing
tools.description: Size the maximum loan under any combination of max LTV, min DSCR, and min debt yield for a given NOI, rate, and amortization. Reports the binding constraint, debt service, and resulting metrics; optionally a stress table over NOI, rate, and value shocks (max loan, binding constraint, LTV, DSCR, debt yield per scenario) and the refinance shortfall against an existing loan balance. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.debt_sizing@3 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

value.description: Appraised or underwritten value, USD. Required when max_ltv is set.

min_dscr.description: Minimum debt service coverage ratio, e.g. 1.25.

round_down_to.description: Round the final loan amount down to this increment (lenders often use 1,000 or 10,000).

existing_loan_balance.description: Balance of the loan being refinanced, USD. Adds a refinance result (shortfall or excess proceeds against the max loan) and a shortfall per stress scenario.

stress.description: Stress table: every combination of the NOI, rate, and value shocks (up to 1,000 scenarios), each sized under the same constraints and rounding. The base result is unchanged.

noi_shocks.description: Relative NOI changes as decimals, e.g. [-0.05, -0.1, -0.2] for NOI down 5%, 10%, 20%. Omit for no NOI shock.

rate_shocks.description: Absolute changes to rate_annual as decimals, e.g. [0.005, 0.01] for +50 and +100 bp. The stressed rate must stay at or above 0 and below 1. Omit for no rate shock.

value_shocks.description: Relative value changes as decimals, e.g. [-0.1, -0.2]; requires value. Omit for no value shock.

value_moves_with_noi.description: Also scale value by each NOI shock (value × (1 + noi_shock), a constant cap rate), as a lender repricing value on stressed NOI would.

tools.name: calc_lease_remeasurement_asc842
tools.description: Remeasure a lessee's lease liability and right-of-use asset under ASC 842 after a modification, lease-term reassessment, contingency resolution, or residual value guarantee change: new liability (PV of remaining payments), liability and ROU adjustments with any gain (ASC 842-20-35-4), and the per-period amortization table (operating: straight-line single lease cost; finance: interest plus amortization) in cents that foots: every row rolls forward exactly, totals are the row sums, and the final period trues up liability and ROU asset to zero. Warns where judgment is needed. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.lease_remeasurement_asc842@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

classification.description: Lessee classification (ASC 842-10-25-2): operating (single straight-line lease cost) or finance (interest on the liability plus straight-line ROU amortization).

period.description: Period index counted from the remeasurement date (1 = first remaining period).

amount.description: Lease payment due in that period after the event, USD for the period (a monthly amount when periods_per_year is 12, not annualized): fixed and in-substance fixed payments, less incentives receivable (ASC 842-10-30-5).

payments.description: Remaining lease payments after the event, in ascending period order. Periods not listed carry no payment (rent-free).

remaining_periods.description: Remaining lease term in periods after the event. Defaults to the last period index in payments; set it higher when the final periods are rent-free.

payment_timing.description: Whether each payment falls at the beginning (in advance) or end (in arrears) of its period.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate applied to the remaining payments, e.g. 0.06. Nominal: the periodic rate is this ÷ periods_per_year.

periods_per_year.description: Payment periods per year (12 for monthly, 4 for quarterly).

discount_rate_updated.description: True when discount_rate_annual was determined at the remeasurement date (ASC 842-10-35-5: required for modifications and lease-term or purchase-option reassessments); false when it is the rate from commencement (kept for contingency resolutions and residual value guarantee changes).

liability_before.description: Carrying amount of the lease liability immediately before the remeasurement, USD.

rou_asset_before.description: Carrying amount of the right-of-use asset immediately before the remeasurement, USD (after any impairment).

event.description: What triggered the remeasurement: modification_extend_term / modification_shorten_term / modification_change_in_payments (a modification not accounted for as a separate contract, ASC 842-10-25-8 and 25-11), reassessment_of_term_or_option (ASC 842-10-35-1 and 35-4(c)), contingency_resolved (variable payments became fixed, ASC 842-10-35-4(b)), residual_value_guarantee_change (ASC 842-10-35-4(c)(3)), or index_or_rate_change (ASC 842-10-35-4: not a remeasurement trigger by itself; computed as if remeasured for another reason).

tools.name: calc_prepayment_and_defeasance
tools.description: Prepayment premium, total payoff, and cost as a share of balance for a fixed-rate amortizing or interest-only loan under yield maintenance (PV of remaining payments or rate differential, with a minimum and an explicit discounting convention), a step-down schedule, a flat percentage, or defeasance (cost of the securities portfolio that funds the remaining payments plus stated costs). Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.prepayment_and_defeasance@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

balance.description: Outstanding principal balance at the payoff date, USD.

remaining_term_months.description: Months from the payoff date to the loan's maturity date (the balloon is due with the final payment).

amortization_months.description: Remaining amortization basis in months at the payoff date (e.g. 300 for a 30-year schedule with 5 years elapsed); 0 for interest-only. Must be at least remaining_term_months.

accrued_interest.description: Accrued but unpaid interest to the payoff date, USD; added to the total payoff.

treasury_rate_annual.description: Yield on the reference Treasury (usually the one maturing closest to the loan's maturity), e.g. 0.041.

spread_annual.description: Spread added to the Treasury yield for discounting, e.g. 0.005 when the note says 'Treasury plus 50 basis points'. Default 0 (Treasury flat).

minimum_pct.description: Minimum premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.01 for a 1% floor (default). 0 for no floor.

basis.description: pv_of_payments (default): premium = PV of the remaining scheduled payments at the discount rate − balance. rate_differential: premium = PV of (note rate − discount rate) ÷ 12 × scheduled balance for each remaining month.

discount_convention.description: Compounding convention for the discount rate. monthly (default): monthly rate = annual ÷ 12. semiannual: annual is a bond-equivalent yield, monthly rate = (1 + annual ÷ 2)^(1/6) − 1. Lenders differ; read the note.

oneOf.description: Yield maintenance.

loan_month.description: Loan month (1 = first month after origination) in which the payoff occurs.

through_month.description: Last loan month in which this percentage applies.

pct.description: Premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.05 for 5%.

schedule.description: Step-down schedule in ascending through_month order, e.g. 5-4-3-2-1. After the last through_month the loan is open (0%).

oneOf.description: Step-down (declining percentage) premium.

pct.description: Premium as a fraction of the balance, e.g. 0.02.

oneOf.description: Flat percentage premium.

anyOf.description: One flat annual yield for all replacement securities.

months.description: Months from the payoff date up to and including which this yield applies; points in ascending order.

rate.description: Annual yield on replacement securities maturing at or before that month, e.g. 0.042.

anyOf.description: Yield curve as a step function: each payment uses the first point whose months ≥ its month; beyond the last point, the last rate.

replacement_yield.description: Yield on the government securities bought to fund the remaining payments: a flat annual rate, or a list of {months, rate} points.

costs.description: Stated transaction costs, USD: defeasance consultant, legal, accountant, rating agency, servicer and custodian fees.

discount_convention.description: Compounding convention for the discount rate. monthly (default): monthly rate = annual ÷ 12. semiannual: annual is a bond-equivalent yield, monthly rate = (1 + annual ÷ 2)^(1/6) − 1. Lenders differ; read the note.

oneOf.description: Defeasance: buy securities that replicate the remaining payments.

tools.name: calc_walt
tools.description: Weighted average remaining lease term in years as of a date (actual days ÷ 365.25), weighted by each lease's area_sf (weight_by "area") or annual_rent (weight_by "rent"). Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.walt@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

as_of.description: Date to measure remaining term from, YYYY-MM-DD.

weight_by.description: How each lease is weighted: "area" uses its area_sf, "rent" its annual_rent (that field is then required on every lease). Default "area".

id.description: Your identifier for the lease (ideally a FactLot lease ID).

area_sf.description: Leased square feet (required when weight_by is area).

annual_rent.description: Current annual rent, USD per year (required when weight_by is rent).

leases.description: Leases in the portfolio or building.

tools.name: calc_npv
tools.description: NPV of periodic cash flows (t = 0, 1, 2, ...; the t = 0 flow is not discounted) at a per-period discount rate given as a decimal. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.npv@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

cash_flows.description: Periodic cash flows at t = 0, 1, 2, …; negative for outflows (e.g. purchase price at t = 0). At most 10000.

rate.description: Discount rate per period as a decimal, e.g. 0.08 for 8%. Match the cash-flow period: for monthly flows pass the monthly rate (e.g. 0.06 ÷ 12 = 0.005).

tools.name: calc_irr
tools.description: Periodic and annualized IRR of periodic cash flows, as decimals (0.085 = 8.5%), solved deterministically by scanning a 1-point grid of per-period rates and bisecting each sign change; reports every root it finds when cash flows have multiple IRRs (two roots within one grid step can be missed). Errors when the flows do not change sign or no root lies between -99.99% and 1000% per period. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.irr@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

cash_flows.description: Periodic cash flows at t = 0, 1, 2, …; negative for outflows (e.g. purchase price at t = 0). At most 1200.

periods_per_year.description: Cash-flow periods per year, used only to annualize the result: 1 for annual flows, 4 for quarterly, 12 for monthly.

tools.name: calc_lease_vs_own
tools.description: Compare leasing with buying over a fixed horizon: NPV of each case's annual cash costs (rent, free rent, tenant expenses, and move-in costs versus equity, debt service, owner expenses, reserves, and a sale at the horizon by stated value or exit cap rate), optionally after tax, with the year-by-year tables and the break-even residual value at which owning equals leasing. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.lease_vs_own@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

horizon_years.description: Analysis horizon in years. Both cases are compared over this period; the own case sells at the end of it.

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08, applied to both cases' year-end cash flows (year 0 = closing / move-in).

annual_rent.description: Rent due in each year of the horizon, USD, year 1 first. Must have exactly horizon_years entries.

oneOf.description: Explicit rent per year.

escalation_rate_annual.description: Compounding annual bump, e.g. 0.03: rent_k = base × (1 + e)^(k − 1).

oneOf.description: Base rent with a compounding annual escalation.

rent.description: Annual rent, as an explicit schedule or base rent with escalation.

free_rent_months.description: Rent-free months at the start of the lease, abated from year 1 (and year 2 if more than 12). Must not exceed the horizon.

operating_expenses_annual.description: Year-1 operating expenses borne by the tenant on top of rent (NNN charges, utilities), USD per year.

expense_growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth applied to expenses after year 1, e.g. 0.03 (year k = year-1 amount × (1 + g)^(k − 1)).

upfront_costs.description: Tenant's one-time costs at move-in not covered by allowances: TI overage, moving, security deposit treated as cost, USD.

closing_costs.description: Acquisition closing costs, USD (added to the purchase price for cash and for depreciable basis).

loan.description: Acquisition financing. Omit for an all-cash purchase.

amortization_years.description: Amortization in years with monthly payments; 0 means interest-only. Any balance outstanding at the horizon is repaid from sale proceeds.

operating_expenses_annual.description: Year-1 operating expenses borne by the owner (utilities, repairs, management), USD per year.

capex_reserve_annual.description: Year-1 capital reserve, USD per year. Treated as a cash cost; not tax-deductible.

property_taxes_annual.description: Year-1 property taxes, USD per year.

insurance_annual.description: Year-1 property insurance, USD per year.

expense_growth_rate_annual.description: Annual growth applied to expenses after year 1, e.g. 0.03 (year k = year-1 amount × (1 + g)^(k − 1)).

amount.description: Expected gross sale price at the end of the horizon, USD.

oneOf.description: A stated residual value.

stabilized_noi.description: Stabilized NOI the property would earn if leased at market in the year after the horizon, USD per year.

oneOf.description: Residual = stabilized NOI ÷ exit cap rate (direct capitalization).

residual.description: How the sale price at the horizon is set.

selling_costs_rate.description: Brokerage and closing costs on sale as a share of the sale price, e.g. 0.03.

tax.description: Optional after-tax comparison. When omitted (the default), both cases are compared pre-tax. Operating expenses, property taxes, and insurance are always deductible when this block is present; the gain on sale is taxed at the marginal rate (no separate recapture rate).

marginal_tax_rate.description: Combined marginal income tax rate applied to deductions and to the gain on sale, e.g. 0.26.

depreciation_life_years.description: Straight-line depreciation life for the building (39 for US non-residential real property). No mid-month convention.

land_share.description: Share of purchase price plus closing costs allocated to land, which is not depreciated.

rent_deductible.description: Whether rent paid in the lease case is deductible (true for an operating business).

interest_deductible.description: Whether loan interest in the own case is deductible.

depreciation_deductible.description: Whether depreciation in the own case is deductible.

tools.name: calc_renew_vs_relocate
tools.description: Compare renewing in place with moving over one horizon: NPV and discounted effective rent of each case (rent schedule with free rent, TI net of allowance, fees, moving, downtime, double rent, termination, and disruption costs), the starting rent at which they break even, and year-by-year cash flows. Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.renew_vs_relocate@2 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

horizon_months.description: Analysis horizon in months; both cases run for this term (e.g. 120 for a ten-year renewal versus a ten-year new lease).

discount_rate_annual.description: Annual discount rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08, applied to both cases (monthly rate = annual ÷ 12).

current_rent_monthly.description: Total monthly rent under the existing lease, USD per month for the whole premises (not $/SF). Prices the double-rent overlap in the relocate case.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5.

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

rate.description: Bump as a decimal, e.g. 0.03 for 3%. Bumps compound.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

schedule.description: Renewal rent terms: commencement date, area, starting $/SF/yr, escalation, and abated (free) months. The term is horizon_months.

ti_cost.description: Refurbishment or TI the tenant would spend on the current premises at renewal, USD, before any allowance.

ti_allowance.description: Landlord renewal allowance, USD. Offsets ti_cost; any excess is not paid out.

renewal_fee.description: Fees to renew (legal, brokerage paid by tenant), USD.

renew.description: Stay and renew the existing lease.

commencement_date.description: Rent commencement date, YYYY-MM-DD. Month n starts on this day-of-month (clamped to month end).

starting_rent_psf_annual.description: Year-one base rent in dollars per SF per year (annual, not monthly), e.g. 42.5.

escalation.description: How base rent escalates. Omit for flat rent.

oneOf.description: Flat rent for the whole term.

rate.description: Bump as a decimal, e.g. 0.03 for 3%. Bumps compound.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Percentage bumps: rate_k = starting_rate × (1 + rate)^k.

amount.description: Dollars per SF per year added at each bump, e.g. 0.50.

every_months.description: Months between bumps (12 = annual). The first bump takes effect in month every_months + 1.

oneOf.description: Fixed $/SF bumps: rate_k = starting_rate + amount × k.

abated_months.description: Fully abated (free) months, 1-based from commencement (e.g. [1,2,3] for three months free up front). Each listed month's base rent is zero.

round_rate_to_cents.description: Round each step's $/SF/yr to cents, as many lease rent tables do.

schedule.description: New-premises rent terms: commencement date, area, starting $/SF/yr, escalation, and abated (free) months. The term is horizon_months.

buildout_cost.description: Total cost to build out the new premises, USD, before any allowance.

ti_allowance.description: Landlord TI allowance at the new premises, USD. Offsets buildout_cost; any excess is not paid out.

moving_cost.description: Moving, IT, cabling, signage, and stationery costs, USD.

downtime_months.description: Months the business runs at reduced capacity around the move.

downtime_cost_monthly.description: Cost of a month of downtime (lost margin, temporary space), USD per month. Multiplied by downtime_months.

overlap_months.description: Months of double rent: the old premises are still paid (at current_rent_monthly) after the new lease starts.

termination_cost.description: Early termination fee, holdover premium, or restoration obligation at the old premises, USD.

disruption_cost.description: Explicit one-time cost of business disruption beyond rent and downtime (lost customers, staff turnover), USD.

tools.name: calc_hotel_metrics
tools.description: Occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, TRevPAR, and a USALI-style profit ladder for a period: departmental profit, GOP and margin, GOPPAR, management fees, EBITDA, FF&E reserve, and NOI (EBITDA less replacement reserve). Deterministic: use this instead of doing the math yourself; cite formula calc.hotel_metrics@1 and the returned steps, and surface any warnings.

nights.description: Nights in the period, e.g. 365 for a year or 30 for a month.

rooms_out_of_order.description: Room-nights (rooms × nights, not rooms) taken off the market in the period, e.g. 20 rooms closed for a 30-night renovation = 600. Subtracted from rooms × nights to give rooms available. USALI (11th ed.) keeps short-term out-of-order rooms in rooms available; include only rooms formally removed from sale.

rooms_sold.description: Room-nights occupied by paying guests in the period (USALI: rooms sold, excluding complimentary rooms).

room_revenue.description: Rooms revenue for the period, USD (USALI Rooms department revenue, net of taxes and allowances).

fb_revenue.description: Food and beverage revenue, USD (USALI Food and Beverage department revenue).

other_revenue.description: Other operated departments plus miscellaneous income, USD (USALI Other Operated Departments and Miscellaneous Income).

departmental_expenses.description: Total departmental expenses, USD: rooms, F&B, and other operated departments (USALI Total Departmental Expenses).

undistributed_expenses.description: Total undistributed operating expenses, USD: administrative and general, information and telecommunications, sales and marketing, property operation and maintenance, utilities (USALI Total Undistributed Operating Expenses).

management_fee_rate.description: Base management fee as a share of total operating revenue, e.g. 0.03 (USALI Management Fees).

management_fee_fixed.description: Fixed or incentive management fee for the period, USD, added to the percentage fee (USALI Management Fees).

non_operating_expenses.description: Property taxes, insurance, ground rent, and other non-operating expenses, USD (USALI Non-Operating Income and Expenses).

ffe_reserve_rate.description: FF&E replacement reserve as a share of total operating revenue, e.g. 0.04 (USALI Replacement Reserve, below EBITDA).

tools.name: rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline
tools.description: Deadline to file a Texas property tax protest with the appraisal review board: the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice of appraised value was delivered, rolled past weekends and Texas legal holidays, plus a conservative file-by date. Returns the statute citations and the rule's verification status. Verification status: verified. Cite rule rules.tx.property_tax_protest_deadline@1 and its statutes.

notice_delivered_date.description: Date the appraisal district's notice of appraised value was delivered (Tax Code §25.19), YYYY-MM-DD. A mailed notice is presumed delivered on the day it was deposited in the mail (§1.07(c)). Omit if unknown (May 15 is then the only basis).

tools.name: id_parcel
tools.description: Deterministic FactLot ID for a parcel from state FIPS, county FIPS, and the assessor's parcel number (APN). The same parcel always yields the same ID, offline. Use it as the join key across systems.

state_fips.description: 2-digit state FIPS code, e.g. "06" for California.

county_fips.description: 3-digit county FIPS code, e.g. "037" for Los Angeles County.

apn.description: Assessor's parcel number exactly as the county prints it; formatting is normalized.

tools.name: id_entity
tools.description: Deterministic FactLot ID for a legal entity (LLC, LP, corporation, trust) from its registry jurisdiction and file number, or from its LEI.

jurisdiction.description: Registry jurisdiction, e.g. "us-de" for Delaware, or "lei" for a Legal Entity Identifier.

registry_number.description: File number issued by that registry, or the 20-character LEI.

tools.name: id_space
tools.description: FactLot ID for a suite or unit within a building, given the building's FactLot URN. Suite designators are normalized.

suite.description: Suite or unit as written ("Suite 400", "STE 400", "#400", "3rd Floor" all normalize).

tools.name: id_document
tools.description: Content-addressed FactLot ID (SHA-256) for a document such as a lease, amendment, or estoppel.

content_base64.description: Base64 of the exact file bytes (preferred: every party gets the same ID).

text.description: Document text, UTF-8 encoded before hashing. Use only when bytes are unavailable.

tools.name: id_parse
tools.description: Validate a FactLot URN and return its kind, components, and short ID.

urn.description: A FactLot URN to validate, e.g. fl:parcel:us-06037:5432001012.

tools.name: fact_validate
tools.description: Check that a fact conforms to the FactLot model (subject ID, dotted predicate, as_of date, provenance with citations, optional AI-use rights). Returns { valid, issues }. Call before storing or sharing extracted facts.

fact.description: A FactLot fact: subject, predicate, value, as_of, provenance (with sources), optional rights.

tools.name: registry_get
tools.description: Everything the FactLot Registry knows about a parcel or legal entity: status, current cited facts (owner of record, situs address, property category, areas, values), ownership links, and external IDs. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

urn.description: FactLot URN of a parcel or entity, e.g. fl:parcel:us-48201:0420150000012.

include_history.description: Also return superseded facts from earlier snapshots.

tools.name: registry_resolve_parcel
tools.description: Find a parcel's FactLot URN from state FIPS, county FIPS, and APN, if the registry holds it. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

county_fips.description: 3-digit county FIPS, e.g. "201" for Harris County.

apn.description: Parcel or account number as the county prints it.

tools.name: registry_resolve_external
tools.description: Find the FactLot URN for an ID from another system, e.g. system "tx-harris-cad-account" or "us-tx-taxpayer". Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

tools.name: registry_search_address
tools.description: Find commercial parcels by situs address (normalized: 'Street' = 'St', 'Suite' = 'Ste'). Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

query.description: Street address or part of one.

tools.name: registry_search_entities
tools.description: Find registered business entities (LLCs, LPs, corporations) by name. Natural persons are not searchable. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

query.description: Entity name or part of one.

tools.name: registry_owned_by
tools.description: Commercial parcels currently linked to a legal entity as owner of record (inferred links carry a confidence). Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).
